content:
Alex: Quick sync — SDK question re 429 semantics for per-route quotas. Do we want SDKs to treat X-RateLimit-Remaining as strictly per-route (when X-Route-ID present) vs a global bucket? Also what should clients do on a 'soft-429' (we've discussed returning 429 but signaling it's advisory)? Need a short contract I can reference in the SDK PR.

Priya: TL;DR: treat X-Route-ID as authoritative for per-route limits. If X-Route-ID missing, fall back to global. Soft-429s = advisory: runtime may return 429 with X-Soft-429: true when load is high but not catastrophic. Clients should do short backoff + try fallback rather than hard-stop. We'll publish the header semantics in the API doc.

Jonah: Implementation note from runtime side: we can emit both headers + body, but want to avoid breaking older clients. Current plan: include headers always and add a small JSON body for new clients: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 2
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 2351234667
X-Route-ID: text.generate.v1
X-Soft-429: true
Content-Type: application/json

{"type":"soft","hint":"try-fallback-or-backoff"}
```

Kira: SDK concerns: older SDKs only look for Retry-After. New semantics need heuristics so we don't break. Proposal for SDKs:
- If Retry-After present, honor it.
- If X-Soft-429: true and Retry-After missing or <=3s, treat as advisory: do a short base backoff (base=500ms) with 3 tries, then attempt fallback model/route.
- If X-Soft-429 not present (hard 429), apply longer exponential backoff and surface error to user.

Example pseudo: `wait = min(60, 0.5 * 2**attempt)` and if soft then cap attempts at 3 and then try fallback.

Priya: +1 to Kira's heuristics. Add: SDK should expose a callback/hook so app can decide to queue/partial-respond rather than just retry. Document recommended fallback order: lower-q model -> smaller batch -> reproximate async job.

Emma: QA checklist for this contract:
- Verify headers present for both soft and hard 429s.
- Confirm X-Route-ID appears for per-route limits.
- Validate SDK behavior matrix: old SDK (Retry-After only), new SDK (heuristics + hooks), no-Route-ID case.
- Load test: simulate rapid burst from single API key and ensure either soft-429s appear before hard 429s.

Jonah: runtime note: for per-user bursting we use a token-lease window; soft-429 emitted when bucket dipping below low-watermark. We'll attach a debug flag that includes `X-Burst-Peek` for internal canary only. Not for public doc.

Kira: One more backwards-compatibility edge: some clients parse X-RateLimit-Reset as epoch seconds. Confirm that's what we'll ship (not ms).

Priya: Confirmed: X-RateLimit-Reset = unix epoch seconds. We'll avoid ms to reduce client bugs.

Alex: Small UX ask: can we make the advisory text machine-readable (we already proposed JSON body). If runtime adds {"type":"soft","action":"fallback:lower-model"} clients can automate.

Jonah: We can add an `action` field but keep it opt-in in body for now. Headers remain the contract. Body is optional augmentation.

DevBot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for rate-limit changes (canary pool 5%): infra-change-id=rl-2026-03-17-1. Logs will include X-Burst-Peek for canary.

Kira: I'll update SDK PR: implement heuristics + expose onRetryHook for apps. Will include unit tests for header parsing and a small integration test hitting canary.

Emma: I'll add QA job with steps and a small harness to assert soft->hard transition under sustained load.

Alex: Awesome, thanks everyone. I'll draft the API blurb and link to SDK PR. @Kira pls ping when PR is ready so we can merge with docs. :thumbsup:
